thread.title: Google Vs. Apple: There Is A Clear Winner - Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL)

author: Mauro Solis
title: Google Vs. Apple: There Is A Clear Winner - Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL)
text:
Warren Buffett recently bought 75 million Apple ( AAPL ) shares for Berkshire Hathaway ( BRK.A ) ( BRK.B ). He criticized investors and analysts that invest by trying to guess the number of iPhones that Apple will sell next quarter, as they are missing the long-term view of the company.
The idea of spending loads of time trying to guess how many iPhone Xs or whatever it may be are going to be sold in a given three-month period of time, to me it totally misses the point. (...) Nobody buys a farm based on whether they think it's going to rain next year or not. They buy it because they think it's a good investment over 10 or 20 years."
-Warren Buffett.
I agree with most of what Buffett said, but I think he bought the wrong farm.
3 Big changes are coming to technology in the following years. AI, IOT and the other half of the population getting Internet. Looking at Apple and Google ( GOOG ) ( GOOGL ), it is difficult to see a trend where Apple goes on top in 5years. Apple is undeniably a great company. Their brand is excellent, their products are well designed, and they have a healthy relationship with their customers. However, their innovation and growth prospects are limited. Google not only has a bigger and better moat, but it also has the siege power to take on a big part of Apple's strengths.
The three big changes 1.- Let's compare Apple's progress in Artificial intelligence with Google's. Between Google's Deepmind and Tensorflow, Google has a superior platform for developing AI, Apple's progress is not negligible, but it is behind far behind Google.
Apple's culture is also proving to be a disadvantage here, many AI experts aim to publish their work, and Apple policies are very restricting. Being able to attract the best talent is especially crucial for AI since the number of experts is scarce and there is high demand for them. Apple has been loosening the strings on this point, but it is still in disadvantage.
